name: FunctionQA
intro: FunctionQA 是 MathVista 新建的 400 题视觉代数子集，考查函数图精细感知以及变量、表达式、方程和函数上的代数推理。论文只对三套新数据共 736 题汇总披露人工标注与三人复核，并未单独公开 FunctionQA 的更细题源。固定数据版本含 testmini 62 题和隐藏答案的 test 338 题。
org: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research
build_method: STEM 研究生人工标注, 三人复核新数据, 共识消歧, FunctionQA 细粒度题源未披露
task_type: 函数图问答, 视觉代数推理
eval_feature: 题型提示, 短答案抽取, 选择题最近选项匹配, 数值归一化, 精确准确率
build_method_en: STEM graduate-student annotation, three-reviewer checking of the new datasets, consensus resolution, finer FunctionQA provenance undisclosed
eval_feature_en: Question-type Prompting, Short-answer Extraction, Nearest-choice Matching, Numeric Normalization, Exact Accuracy
intro_en: FunctionQA is MathVista's newly created 400-item visual-algebra subset. It tests fine-grained perception of function plots and algebra over variables, expressions, equations, and functions. The paper reports annotation and three-reviewer checking only in aggregate for all 736 newly created MathVista items, not FunctionQA-specific item provenance. The pinned data revision has 62 testmini and 338 hidden-answer test items.

drawio_review_note: Reviewed against MathVista arXiv:2310.02255v3, official repository commit 53d525874bdde205128e6b160b7357a88277d479, and AI4Math/MathVista dataset revision 2b6ad69445fbb5695c9b165475e8decdbeb97747. FunctionQA is the 400-item MathVista visual-algebra subset. The paper says STEM graduate students annotate the new datasets and three reviewers independently check them; 99.2% agreement and six consensus-resolved answer disagreements are aggregate results for all 736 new MathVista items, not FunctionQA-only statistics. Finer FunctionQA image and item-authoring provenance is not disclosed. The pinned release contains 62 testmini and 338 test items; answer types are 263 multiple-choice/text, 132 free-form integer, and 5 free-form float. The pinned evaluator uses exact type fast paths or a few-shot GPT-4 extractor, then nearest-choice matching for multiple choice, integer casting, precision-aware float rounding, exact normalized-string comparison, and average/fine-grained accuracy.
